pr_title: Setting to disable x-opaque-id in logs throttling
pr_body:
Introduces a setting cluster.deprecation_indexing.x_opaque_id_used.enabled to disable use of
x-opaque-id in RateLimitingFilter. This will be used for deprecation
logs indexing and will not affect logging to files (it uses different
instance of RateLimitingFilter with this flag enabled by default)

Changes the indices backing a deprecation log data stream to be hidden.

Refactors DeprecationHttpIT to be more reliable

relates #76292
closes #77936

issue_context.title: Document "cluster.deprecation_indexing.enabled"
issue_context.body:
I can't seem to find any documentation for "cluster.deprecation_indexing.enabled" which enables writing the deprecation logs to a data stream. I would expect to see the documentation at https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.x/logging.html#deprecation-logging and have it mention that is will write the logs to a data stream named '.logs-deprecation.elasticsearch-default' as well as something about enabling this for the Kibana upgrade assistant. 

related: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/46106

cc @pugnascotia @pgomulka

review_comments:
@pugnascotia addressing https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/78319/files#r723033047 here
I think it is fine (other tests log those documents too). We only store the server logs when a test failed. So this will help to debug why the test failed
Actually, if we're asserting on the documents, the assertion failure will be in the build scan, so are we sure we need this logged as well?
yes, the assertion failure logs both expected and actual collections, but to me the assertion output for collection is not super clear.. Happy to remove that logger.warn if you think otherwise
I don't really mind, it just seemed a bit redundant.
I wonder if we should be disabling this setting in an `@After` method?
good idea. Btw this line I think it should stay as I am trying to confirm that the second deprecation won't be logged after the setting is turned off.

```suggestion
 * This filter works by using an LRU cache with 128 entries. When a cache miss occurs,
 * the oldest entries are removed.
```

You could also link to: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cache_replacement_policies#Least_recently_used_(LRU)
I feel like a link to this article might be too detailed (merged the suggestion)
